w: Ground broke here in 1782, the day Rama I shifted the capital across the river from Thonburi and founded the Chakri dynasty. Kings ruled from within these walls until 1925; the court is long gone, but state ceremonies still fill the grounds, drawing some eight million visitors a year.
s: Where five reigns of Chakri kings held court
_facts: Complex of buildings at the heart of Bangkok
Official residence of Kings of Siam/Thailand since 1782
Court based here until 1925
Construction began 6 May 1782 under Rama I after moving the capital from Thonburi
Expanded especially under Rama V
Over eight million visitors a year
Still used for royal ceremonies and state functions

w: Chulalongkorn University's urban design centre turned the abandoned concrete of the Lavalin Skytrain project -- a rail line cancelled mid-build in the 1990s -- into a 280-metre elevated walkway over the Chao Phraya. Opened in 2020, it is billed as the first sky park in Southeast Asia, built on someone else's failure.
s: An elevated park grown on a cancelled 1990s Skytrain
_facts: Elevated linear park built on the central viaduct of the failed Lavalin Skytrain project
About 280m long
Designed by Urban Design and Development Center, Chulalongkorn University
Opened June 2020
Considered the first sky park in Southeast Asia

w: The gilded, dragon-prowed barges of the Royal Barge Procession live in what used to be a working dry dock on Bangkok Noi canal. Allied bombing badly damaged both dock and boats during the Second World War; the Fine Arts Department restored them in 1949, and the site became a museum in 1972.
s: Royal ceremonial barges docked in a bombed-out shipyard
_facts: Museum on the northern rim of Bangkok Noi canal
Houses barges from the Royal Barge Procession
Formerly a dry dock for barges and warships under the Bureau of the Royal Household and Royal Thai Navy
Sustained severe bombing damage in WWII
Restored 1949 by the Fine Arts Department
Became the National Museum of Royal Barges in 1972

w: Tucked inside the Grand Palace walls, this museum occupies the 1873 Ratsadakorn-bhibhathana Building -- once home to the Royal Treasury Ministry and the original Crown Property Bureau. Queen Sirikit requested its conversion in 2003, turning a revenue office into a showcase for Thai textile craft.
s: A Grand Palace revenue office turned textile museum
_facts: Museum inside the Grand Palace grounds
Occupies the 1873 Ratsadakorn-bhibhathana Building, formerly of the Royal Treasury Ministry
Building was the original home of the Crown Property Bureau
Converted at Queen Sirikit's request in 2003

w: Built in 1881 for the Chinese-Thai trader Tan Siew-Wang, this U-shaped courtyard house on the Chao Phraya riverbank was modelled on his wife's family home. It anchors the Wanglee dynasty's rise in Bangkok trade, and picked up an ASA architectural conservation award in 1984 for staying so intact.
s: An 1881 courtyard house behind a Chinese-Thai trading empire
_facts: Historic building on the west bank of the Chao Phraya in Khlong San district
Built 1881 for Tan Siew-Wang, founder of the Wanglee family
Modified Chinese courtyard house, two storeys, U-shaped plan
Styled on the Poshyananda family home, his wife's family
Received the ASA Architectural Conservation Award in 1984
